traits.notes: The seedling displays distinct trifoliate leaves with alternate leaflet arrangement. There is minor physical damage visible on the margins of some leaves (holes present).

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced apart along the elongated stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaves are composed of multiple distinct leaflets attached to a rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf has a terminal leaflet at the tip of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 3 (most clearly visible leaves are trifoliate with three leaflets)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (the leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in pairs)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins are smooth and continuous)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are lance-shaped, widest below the middle and tapering to a point)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tips taper to a distinct, slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf bases are wedge-shaped, tapering towards the petiolule)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible (secondary veins are clearly visible, curving towards the leaf margin and spaced relatively closely)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces reflect light, appearing glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (leaf surfaces appear smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis and petiolules are elongated relative to the leaflet size)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles and rachis appear round in cross-section, lacking wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stems appear green, thin, and flexible)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: green (stems are uniformly green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stems appear smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: The seedling displays distinct trifoliate leaves with alternate leaflet arrangement. There is minor physical damage visible on the margins of some leaves (holes present).
